summary: Backfill: client liveness, recovery diagnostics, OMP admission cache key, Home Manager memory options, terminal tab input, resync backoff

replay.detail: None of #1587, #1593, #1559, #1602, #1489 or #1618 changes what is projected or triggers a replay or rebuild.

schema.detail: None changes database tables, columns, indexes, triggers or the schema version.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged by all six.

compatibility.detail: #1489 (terminal tab input): one new, empty PTY frame, accepted only from an attached writer, carries the stuck-key recovery; an older PTY daemon ignores it, so the recovery key does nothing there; it also moves the pty pin. #1559 (OMP admission): the admission cache key changes with the probe code, so old failed records need no cleanup. #1587 (client liveness from the stream) and #1618 (resync re-ask backoff in stui and the phone) are client-side: no wire change. #1593 only changes recovery diagnostics in a test and its eval script.

downtime.detail: No additional service interruption beyond the ordinary restart from any of the six.

manual.detail: #1602 adds Nix Home Manager options for the daemon's memory limits: no runtime change, but a deployer who wants the limits must use the new options. None of the other five needs a manual step.

recovery.detail: No database or runtime recovery change from any of the six; older builds ignore the changes (an older PTY daemon ignores the new frame).
